newsitem.title: UK: UK's C4 rejoices as privatisation threat fades.
newsitem.headline: UK's C4 rejoices as privatisation threat fades.

text.p: Britain's Channel 4 television breathed a sigh of relief on Wednesday as the threat of privatisation receded.
The UK government's Budget Red Book makes no mention of any funds from a Channel 4 sale -- indicating that the immediate threat of privatisation has been lifted.
"We are very pleased to have got over this hurdle and the indication is that the impetus towards privatisation has slowed right down in recent months," said a Channel 4 spokesman.
Channel 4 chief executive Michael Grade has argued long and and hard against privatisation after the possibility was first raised by members of the ruling Conservative party.
His case appears to have won strong backing from National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley, the minister responsible for broadcasting.

A Conservative party spokeswoman would not be drawn on whether a commitment to privatise Channel 4 would be included in the party's manifesto for the general election due by next May. She said that such issues were currently being reviewed.
The opposition Labour Party oppose a privatisation which some media analysts say could raise 2-3 billion stg.

Channel 4, launched in 1982, is a public service corporation funded by the income from advertising. It has a special remit to innovate and experiment and to appeal to tastes not generally catered for by the commercial ITV network.
It has given strong support to British cinema and has been involved in the production of hit films such as "Four Weddings And A Funeral" and "Trainspotting".
